A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 18-page paper, including Appendices A–C. Text, figures, tables, equations, and rendered pages support a reliable comparison; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link.

before.justification: v2 reports original weather-effect experiments on five 3D scenes, including quantitative baseline comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–6 and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical comparisons, ablations, trajectory-drift measurements, and qualitative results in Section 4 and Appendices A and C.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B describe identical MPM motion priors, recurrent neural dynamics models, Video-SDS objectives, adaptive regularization, and collision-handling procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use Garden, Bicycle, and Stump from Mip-NeRF360 and Playground and Truck from Tanks and Temples. Snowfall, rainfall, fog, sandstorms, and creative appearance variations are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain ClimateNeRF and GaussCtrl in Table 1 and Instruct-4DGS in Appendix A, Table 3. Their participation in the corresponding qualitative comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics and settings are identical, including 15 camera trajectories per scene, evaluation images from training viewpoints, and the optimization settings documented in Appendix B.

E4.justification: Both retain the four component ablations in Section 4.3 and the adaptive-weight, individual-regularization-loss, and trajectory-drift analyses in Appendix A, with identical evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both present aggregate scores and average drift without reporting repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and qualitative results match. For example, the method's all-effects CLIPSim remains 0.28 in Table 1, and its average trajectory drift remains 0.24 in Table 6.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), including the recurrent updates, regularization objectives, and average-drift definition, are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about physics-guided joint motion and appearance optimization, continuous particle emission, and experimental superiority.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including the discussion of bidirectional interactions, static-scene appearance changes, and unreliable physics guidance when learned trajectories drift too far.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical implementation details, hyperparameters, simulation settings, initialization prompts, hardware, runtime, and code references. The project URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 40 references and related-work discussion appear in both versions, with unchanged positioning relative to static editing, 4D generation/editing, and physics-based animation.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 27 November 2025 to v3 dated 17 March 2026. The paper's wording, title, authors, section structure, and appendix organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: All 12 figures and six tables retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Rendered pages 2–18 are pixel-identical; the first-page difference is confined to the administrative stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and appendices are identical. Updating only the arXiv version/date stamp and its link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
